notes.account: The author heads the page Proposition and writes that the two displayed sets C_{>=x} and C_{<=x} are totally ordered, using the underlined abbreviation tot with a raised t/l. The next paragraph says it is enough to prove the first, with the explicit parenthetical phrase “par dualité”. The opposite order directions in the two displayed definitions were read directly from the ink; the text’s duality reference helped locate the intended pair without supplying any symbol.

The author gives the displayed wording “Si x<y, x<z, avec y≠z” and “alors (y,z) comparables.” The sketch beside the subsequent note has the labelled lower x and upper y,z, plus an unlabeled upper-centre point and four upward arrowheads. The drawing was traced as the visible marks; no relation for the extra point or fragments is asserted.

The bracketed note says y and z are “non congrus mod sigma, à cause de 28 a),”. The lower text then discusses y,z being incomparables and states that sigma y and z are comparables. The short word in “On peu/pas/ne peut avoir” remains uncertain. The subsequent written argument uses z<=sigma y and x<=sigma y, calls this a contradiction with x<y by “(28) a)”, and changes a cancelled “ne peut avoir” to the interlinear “aurait donc”. These are the author’s claims and revisions. The phrase “ce qui contredit” was a cue to inspect the short word and signs closely; it was not used to insert a negation or to alter the ink.

The last line reads sigma y<z, “d’où”, then sigma z< and one falling stroke. It does not supply a completed final operand. Most of the lower portion of the paper is blank. No date or explicit question mark is present. The written title is Proposition; 39 at the bottom left is the pencil archive sheet number and is preserved only as a comment. No authorial page number is identified.

Crop 12 resolves the cancelled phrase as “ne peut avoir”: the initial low ne, descending p, small t remnant and later avoir with an i dot survive the horizontal strike. The entire live “aurait donc” lies above it. C and H have the same primary words and acknowledge the replacement; H’s uncertainty on its cancelled phrase alone is not counted as a collation difference.

notes.text: The heading is underlined Proposition. The sheet is handwritten on otherwise blank paper. No date or separate authorial page number is visible. A light-pencil 39 occurs at the bottom left and is retained only as the archive-sheet-number comment.

The author writes the two displayed sets C_{geq x}={y in C | y geq x} and C_{leq x}={y in C | y leq x}, followed by the assertion that they are “tot” with a raised t/l, “ordonnés.” The four non-strict order signs in these definitions have visible lower strokes. This records the source statement without adding a theorem or hypotheses.

The proof setup contains the author’s phrase “(par dualité)”, two raised additions le and pour, and cancelled starters. The subsequent display writes x<y, x<z, y unequal z, followed by “alors (y,z) comparables.” The visible letters, including cel/cela and aussi/ceci, are retained independently of the expected prose.

The bracketed note reads “non congrus mod” sigma and “à cause de 28 a)”. The first reference has no opening parenthesis. The later reference is written “(28) a).” No referenced page was consulted; the reference is recorded as the author wrote it.

The continuation discusses the source’s y,z incomparability and sigma y,z comparability, then uses the phrase “ce qui contredit x<y par (28) a).” This is the author’s argument as written. The heavily retraced comparisons after z and x remain < versus less-than-or-equal uncertain; the argument is not used to decide their extra horizontal strokes.

The lower revision replaces a cancelled ne peut avoir with the raised “aurait donc.” The final line contains sigma y<z, “d’où”, sigma z<, and a single falling diagonal. The diagonal does not complete a readable operand; none has been added. No explicit authorial question or check mark is present on this page.

The diagram is reproduced as an arrow diagram, preserving its three actual solid dots, the z label beside an arrowhead, four rising heads, and the interrupted shaft pieces. The drawing is kept aligned to the left of the bracketed prose.

notes.text: The page begins with the underlined title Proposition. The author gives two displayed sections C_{>=x} and C_{<=x} and writes that they are tot with a raised t/l, ordonnés. The title and conclusion each have a vertical emphasis stroke at the left. No date or author page number is visible; pencil archive number 39 is at bottom left.

The proof setup contains the author’s phrase “Il suffit de ... prouver ... le premier (par dualité)”. Added le and pour, the uncertain lower article, the upper cancelled notons/noter and cancelled Soit donc are represented separately. The displayed target pairs x<y and x<z with y≠z, then writes “alors (y,z) comparables.” This is a source account of the written proof target.

The adjacent sketch has labels z, y and x, three visible solid marks, four arrowheads and several disconnected shaft segments. The unlabelled upper-centre mark is preserved without assigning it an additional mathematical label.

The bracketed observation reads “y et z sont non congrus mod σ, à cause de 28 a),”. The written reference begins directly with 28. Its final mark has a comma tail. The condition referred to is outside this assigned page and was not inspected.

The lower argument juxtaposes z≤σy, x≤σy and the phrase “ce qui contredit x<y par (28) a).” This directed close inspection of both heavy comparison signs. Their lower horizontal traces are recorded. The small word in “On peu|pas|ne peut avoir” remains uncertain; the argument did not supply replacement letters.

The author cancels the lower phrase ne peut avoir and places “aurait donc” above it, then writes σy<z, d’où σz< followed by one falling stroke. The rest of the lower sheet contains no continuation. No complete final operand, further statement, hypothesis or proof check is supplied by this reading.

There is no explicit authorial question or check marker on the page. The incomplete ending, revised verbs and ambiguous small word are the source’s own visible working state. Reading the argument was not entered as a proof verification.
